topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
authors: Hillier, M., Sutton, L., James, L., Mojtahedi, D., Keay, N. and Hind, K.
title: High prevalence and magnitude of rapid weight loss in mixed martial arts athletes
publisher_or_journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
sample_or_method: N = 314 MMA athletes (287 men, 27 women), validated RWL questionnaire
exact_supporting_quote: [Most athletes reported deliberately cutting weight; coaches were the most-cited influence]
what_it_proves: Near-universal weight cutting in MMA; coaches drive nutrition decisions
pitch_claim_supported: Problem: fighters manage weight; coaches are the channel
strength_of_support: strong: largest MMA-specific sample; Durham co-author link

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
title: Extreme rapid weight loss and rapid weight gain observed in UK mixed martial arts athletes preparing for competition
publisher_or_journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
sample_or_method: n = 7 UK MMA athletes, repeated measures, week before competition
exact_supporting_quote: [body mass fell ~8% during RWL; regain ~11.7% in ~32 h after weigh-in]
what_it_proves: UK MMA athletes cut and regain extreme amounts
limitations: Tiny sample; pre-2022 (landmark: only UK MMA field study)

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
title: Prevalence, magnitude and methods of rapid weight loss reported by male mixed martial arts athletes in Ireland
sample_or_method: Online survey, n = 30 male (15 pro, 15 amateur), Dublin
exact_supporting_quote: All but one (97%) of the athletes surveyed lost weight in order to compete, with the average weight loss being 7.9% ± 3.1% of habitual body mass.
what_it_proves: Replicates near-universal cutting in a neighbouring market

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
title: The practice of weight loss in combat sports athletes: a systematic review
sample_or_method: 26 survey studies, 3,994 participants, 14 combat sports; PROSPERO CRD42023487196
exact_supporting_quote: [weight loss is highly prevalent; most lose <5% of body weight in the 7–14 days before competition; sports scientists have little influence]
what_it_proves: Weight loss is near-universal across combat sports; most cuts are moderate; experts rarely involved
pitch_claim_supported: Problem is real across combat sports; coach-led, not dietitian-led
limitations: Survey-based studies; author order to confirm

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
authors: Franchini, E., Brito, C.J. and Artioli, G.G.
title: Weight loss in combat sports: physiological, psychological and performance effects
publisher_or_journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
exact_supporting_quote: [reported a high prevalence (50%) of RWL, regardless the specific combat discipline]
what_it_proves: Classic review of weight-cut prevalence and effects
conflicts_with: Newer MMA-specific data show higher prevalence (88–97%)

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
title: Effects of rapid weight loss on kidney function in combat sport athletes
sample_or_method: PubMed + Web of Science; healthy athletes losing ~5% in ≤1 week; studies from 2005
exact_supporting_quote: Retrieved studies showed that creatinine, blood urea nitrogen and urine specific gravity values were significantly increased after RWL in the majority of the included studies.
what_it_proves: Rapid weight loss stresses the kidneys
pitch_claim_supported: Harm of weight cutting: why safer fuelling matters (no product claim)
limitations: 2021 (only kidney-focused SR found); acute markers, not long-term outcomes

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
authors: De Albuquerque Mauricio, C. et al.
title: Rapid weight loss of up to five percent of the body mass in less than 7 days does not affect physical performance in official Olympic combat athletes with weight classes: a systematic review with meta-analysis
sample_or_method: Meta-analysis of performance outcomes after ≤5% RWL
exact_supporting_quote: [Rapid Weight Loss of Up to Five Percent of the Body Mass in Less Than 7 Days Does Not Affect Physical Performance]
what_it_proves: Small cuts may not hurt performance
pitch_claim_supported: COUNTER-EVIDENCE: moderate cuts may not create a performance problem
limitations: Olympic combat sports, not MMA; ≤5% only

topic: Weight cutting and rapid weight loss in combat sports
authors: Kirk, C., Langan-Evans, C. and Morton, J.P.
title: Worth the weight? Post weigh-in rapid weight gain is not related to winning or losing in professional mixed martial arts
publisher_or_journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
sample_or_method: CSAC events; Bayesian comparison of winners vs losers
exact_supporting_quote: [the magnitude of rapid weight gain does not predict winning or losing in a professional cohort of MMA athletes]
what_it_proves: Regain doesn't predict winning; fighters compete 1–2 divisions above weigh-in weight
pitch_claim_supported: Context: post-weigh-in food is about health, not a winning edge (careful wording)
limitations: Pro, US data; sample size reported inconsistently (62 vs 31 per group)
conflicts_with: IJSNEM 2019 29(1) small study (regain related to success)
